Island_074.settlement_role: Great Cold North stronghold and expedition capital
Island_074.terrain_character: Glacial wilderness, giant-spruce valleys and wind-scoured ridges
Island_074.secondary_feature: Great communal hall, turf-roof compounds, megaliths, protected winter harbor
Island_074.lore_notes: Great Cold North architecture uses huge timber frames on stone plinths, steep snow roofs, low protected entrances and communal halls; imported masonry becomes heavier northern forms.
Island_074.notes: Keep civilization concentrated so the island still reads as vast northern wilderness.

Island_122.settlement_role: Remote ice-harvesting outpost beside ancient ruins
Island_122.secondary_feature: Ice quarry, sled road, megalithic ruin, tiny winter lodge
Island_122.notes: Almost entirely wild. Sparse structures use the Great Cold North hall tradition at miniature scale and make the ancient landscape feel older than the settlement.

Island_073.settlement_role: Frost Marches frontier capital and timber market
Island_073.terrain_character: Snowy taiga frontier, frozen rivers and sheltered valleys
Island_073.secondary_feature: Raised timber market hall, covered streets, watchtowers, fortified inn
Island_073.lore_notes: Frost Marches architecture favors practical timber, raised foundations, deep eaves, enclosed yards and compact market towns; northern hall traditions become smaller civic buildings.
Island_073.notes: Main cultural bridge between the far north and central civilizations.

Island_105.settlement_role: Compact farm villages and winter storehouses
Island_105.secondary_feature: Raised barns, smokehouses, fenced winter yards, roadside shrine
Island_105.notes: Frontier domestic architecture: tightly grouped buildings, covered connections and deep roofs minimize exposure to snow and wind.

Island_132.primary_function: Timber, fur-style goods and northern exchange
Island_132.secondary_feature: Covered bridge, toll hall, timber warehouses, caravan yard
Island_132.notes: Crownlands market planning is visible in the square, but everything is executed in rough Frost Marches timber and defensive enclosure.

Island_125.settlement_role: Hill fort, chapel and winter refuge
Island_125.secondary_feature: Palisaded ridge fort, bell tower, refuge hall, beacon line
Island_125.notes: Austere frontier landmark where Frost Marches carpentry becomes more formal without becoming High Kingdom stone architecture.

Island_106.primary_function: Polar shipping / wreck salvage / ice routes
Island_106.terrain_character: Broken ice coast, berg channels and exposed rocky shores
Island_106.secondary_feature: Enclosed harbor, sea fort, beacon tower, wreck-timber guildhall
Island_106.lore_notes: Shattered Ice Coast architecture uses stone lower walls, timber uppers, narrow storm-resistant profiles, heavy shutters and prestigious salvaged ship timber.
Island_106.notes: The city should visibly face the sea and storms rather than turn inward.

Island_070.secondary_feature: Ice pits, insulated warehouses, sled ramps, compact worker houses
Island_070.notes: Built low and tight to the ground; practical coastal masonry protects timber interiors from wind.

Island_051.secondary_feature: Wreck yards, reclaimed-timber sheds, crane piers, chandlers' lane
Island_051.notes: The region's love of salvaged ship timber is most explicit here; buildings should visibly incorporate mismatched reused hull pieces.

Island_078.settlement_role: Ice sea fort and rescue station
Island_078.secondary_feature: Beacon keep, breakwater, rescue boathouse, signal mast
Island_078.notes: One of the region's clearest fortress silhouettes, designed around visibility and protected access rather than grand civic display.

Island_092.settlement_role: Small fishing villages tucked into lee coves
Island_092.secondary_feature: Fish sheds, smokehouses, narrow piers, storm chapels
Island_092.notes: A quieter vernacular expression of Shattered Ice Coast culture with fewer fortifications but the same heavy shutters and stone bases.

Island_130.settlement_role: Protected shipyard and naval repair town
Island_130.secondary_feature: Covered dry dock, timber slipways, mast yard, fortified warehouse
Island_130.notes: Frost Marches carpentry and Pirate shipyard ideas are borrowed but adapted for ice, enclosed water and extreme weather.

Island_059.secondary_feature: Survey hut, beacon cairns, emergency shelters, ice path markers
Island_059.notes: Intentionally underbuilt; gives the polar coast a genuinely remote stretch between settled ports.

Island_157.settlement_role: Remote cliff monastery and storm observatory
Island_157.secondary_feature: Stone cloister, wind tower, sea chapel, refuge cells
Island_157.notes: A severe coastal monastery using Shattered Ice Coast materials but with High Kingdom vertical influence translated into low storm-resistant forms.

Island_081.settlement_role: Crownlands capital: royal-administrative city, civic center and principal iron/raid complex
Island_081.terrain_character: Fertile central lowlands and defensible civic hills
Island_081.secondary_feature: Palace-citadel, grand market square, civic halls, monumental gatehouses
Island_081.lore_notes: Crownlands architecture uses dressed stone, measured streets, broad arches, courtyards and formal squares; symmetry and planned urban growth define the culture.
Island_081.notes: Formal heart of the central civilization and strongest expression of Crownlands civic architecture.

Island_062.settlement_role: Crownlands fortress island and naval garrison
Island_062.secondary_feature: Arsenal, barracks, fortified harbor, beacon chain
Island_062.notes: Same arches and masonry vocabulary as the capital, but thicker walls, tighter streets and fewer decorative civic spaces.

Island_139.secondary_feature: Formal cloisters, record halls, gardens, ceremonial bridge
Island_139.notes: A quieter Crownlands expression centered on courtyards, cloisters and learned institutions.

Island_082.terrain_character: High mountains, ravines and alpine terraces
Island_082.secondary_feature: Bridge-castle, terraced monastery, monumental stairs, narrow keeps
Island_082.lore_notes: High Kingdom architecture uses monumental vertical stonework, narrow towers, buttressed walls, cliff bridges and terraced monasteries; Crownlands arches become taller and more dramatic.
Island_082.notes: Political and ceremonial center of the mountain civilization rather than a bulk quarry.

Island_099.secondary_feature: Cliff cloisters, observatory tower, hanging gardens, stair pilgrimage
Island_099.notes: The most contemplative High Kingdom island, with settlement stacked vertically around sacred terraces.

Island_153.secondary_feature: Fortified bridge, gate towers, switchback streets, bridge-builders' yard
Island_153.notes: Stone Highlands engineering influences the craft, but the High Kingdom turns it into monumental defensive architecture.

Island_124.settlement_role: Terraced mountain villages and noble estates
Island_124.secondary_feature: Terrace farms, stone inns, hillside chapels, narrow aqueducts
Island_124.notes: Shows everyday High Kingdom life away from castles while retaining steep streets, vertical silhouettes and careful stonework.

Island_076.settlement_role: Hearthlands lake capital and culinary center
Island_076.terrain_character: Lake valleys, wooded hills and sheltered meadows
Island_076.secondary_feature: Great inn, brewery quarter, covered market, lake promenade
Island_076.lore_notes: Hearthlands architecture uses warm timber-and-stone houses, deep porches, broad hearths, gabled inns and dense villages shaped around water.
Island_076.notes: Welcoming water-oriented cultural center for food, brewing and hospitality.

Island_017.secondary_feature: Malt houses, breweries, smokehouses, storage cellars
Island_017.notes: Production stays embedded in a cozy Hearthlands town rather than becoming a factory landscape.

Island_123.settlement_role: Hearthlands farming villages and estate landscape
Island_123.secondary_feature: Orchards, manor farm, cider press, stone field walls
Island_123.notes: Softer and more enclosed agricultural landscape than the open Breadbasket.

Island_145.secondary_feature: Covered bridge, ferry hall, boathouses, waterfront inn
Island_145.notes: Connects Hearthlands to nearby regions while retaining a distinctly domestic Hearthlands scale.

Island_030.settlement_role: Small lakeside abbey and pilgrimage village
Island_030.secondary_feature: Bell tower, cloister garden, hillside path, guesthouse
Island_030.notes: Low-intensity cultural island that gives the region breathing room and history.

Island_084.settlement_role: Timberlands forestry capital and primary tree-production ecosystem
Island_084.terrain_character: Dense production forest and logging valleys
Island_084.secondary_feature: Great sawmill, timber guild hall, log port, monumental frame hall
Island_084.lore_notes: Timberlands architecture celebrates oversized timber frames, exposed joinery, broad roofs, drying lofts and functional towers.
Island_084.notes: Main Wood & Tree island; all tree families stay consolidated in the broader Timberlands system, including Nether wood.

Island_143.secondary_feature: Mill race, log ponds, drying yards, timber warehouses
Island_143.notes: Work-focused Timberlands town dominated by exposed frames and production infrastructure.

Island_140.settlement_role: Craft town for carpenters, joiners and builders
Island_140.secondary_feature: Joinery hall, covered workshop streets, furniture yards
Island_140.notes: Refined side of Timberlands culture: large timber vocabulary used for craftsmanship.

Island_108.settlement_role: Minimal settlement; ranger and forester outposts only
Island_108.secondary_feature: Ancient grove, canopy paths, fire lookout
Island_108.notes: Intentionally underbuilt to preserve the sense of a forest larger than its industry.

Island_109.secondary_feature: Boom chains, cranes, log rafts, warehouse piers
Island_109.notes: Grand Exchange logistics translated into Timberlands timber construction.

Island_012.primary_function: Forestry knowledge / seed and sapling stewardship
Island_012.secondary_feature: Tree library, specimen groves, guild lodge
Island_012.notes: Knowledge center preserving and propagating the complete tree collection.

Island_117.settlement_role: Managed grove communities and specialist nurseries
Island_117.secondary_feature: Distinct grove districts, propagation yards, small lumber camps
Island_117.notes: Separates visually unusual tree families into designed ecosystems while keeping them in one region.

Island_094.secondary_feature: Tall timber fire tower, ranger hut, signal beacon
Island_094.notes: Small architectural punctuation mark rather than a full town.

Island_093.settlement_role: Breadbasket market capital and principal agricultural ecosystem
Island_093.terrain_character: Open farmland, canals and orchard belts
Island_093.secondary_feature: Great granary, central mill, produce market, canal basin
Island_093.lore_notes: Breadbasket architecture uses broad farm compounds, long barns, mills, canal warehouses and durable farmhouses shaped by land and water management.
Island_093.notes: Administrative and market center of large-scale agriculture.

Island_119.settlement_role: Large farm estates, field villages and compost/moss support
Island_119.secondary_feature: Field grids, barns, windmills, composting yards, irrigation works
Island_119.notes: Most openly agricultural island, including bone-meal and moss support loops.

Island_129.secondary_feature: Watermills, lock gates, grain warehouses, barge docks
Island_129.notes: Breadbasket production transitions into trade through canals and mills.

Island_088.settlement_role: Grand Exchange metropolis and principal trade hub
Island_088.terrain_character: Dense harbor district and engineered waterfront
Island_088.secondary_feature: Grand market, guild quarter, customs basin, central warehouses
Island_088.lore_notes: Grand Exchange architecture uses tall mercantile buildings, arcaded quays, warehouse rows and mixed imported materials adapted to dense commerce.
Island_088.notes: Moves goods without replacing the processing ecosystems that belong in producing regions.

Island_020.secondary_feature: Warehouse canyons, cranes, sorter halls, freight yards
Island_020.notes: Highly functional commercial island prioritizing loading access, firebreaks and dense storage.

Island_024.settlement_role: Customs harbor, bonded warehouses and foreign docks
Island_024.secondary_feature: Customs house, quarantine pier, foreign merchants' quarter
Island_024.notes: First contact point for much maritime trade; foreign architectural details are most visible here.

Island_156.secondary_feature: Exchange hall, counting houses, auction court, guild palaces
Island_156.notes: Prestige-commercial satellite with institutions that organize trade and finance.

Island_077.settlement_role: Engineer's Reach city with several distinct engineering districts
Island_077.terrain_character: Industrial terraces, rail cuts and workshop districts
Island_077.secondary_feature: Machine halls, test yards, rail works, component shops, utilities quarter
Island_077.lore_notes: Engineer's Reach architecture uses brick-and-stone industrial shells, long-span roofs, exposed mechanisms, gantries and modular workshop bays.
Island_077.notes: Single-island city-region divided into neighborhoods and technical districts rather than one monolithic factory.

Island_089.settlement_role: Artisan Coast city with specialized craft quarters
Island_089.terrain_character: Bright coastal terraces and artisan quarters
Island_089.secondary_feature: Glassworks, dye quarter, concrete yards, tile workshops, gallery market
Island_089.lore_notes: Artisan Coast architecture uses patterned facades, colored glass, tile and concrete accents, intimate courtyards and street-facing workshops.
Island_089.notes: Production reads as workshops embedded in an inhabited coastal city, not a centralized plant.

Island_075.settlement_role: Fortified Marches capital and principal hostile-mob production center
Island_075.terrain_character: Dark forest edge and defensive clearings
Island_075.secondary_feature: Wall-ring town, ward towers, hunter guild, sealed mobworks district
Island_075.lore_notes: Haunted Marches architecture uses compact defensive compounds, limited windows, heavy shutters, reused masonry, ditches and watch structures.
Island_075.notes: Civilization survives through fortification, ritualized watchkeeping and controlled exploitation of dangerous mobs.

Island_079.settlement_role: Necropolis, ossuary monastery and grave-warden hamlet
Island_079.secondary_feature: Ossuary halls, bell tower, walled cemetery, lantern causeway
Island_079.notes: Defensive Marches architecture becomes inward-facing cloisters and protected burial courts.

Island_104.settlement_role: Powderworks fortress and guarded industrial hamlet
Island_104.secondary_feature: Blast-separated magazines, watch platforms, stone powder vaults
Island_104.notes: Gunpowder production is physically isolated and culturally feared; structures are squat, separated and heavily walled.

Island_120.secondary_feature: Arrow yards, bone storehouses, underground galleries, fortified chapel
Island_120.notes: Turns the region's funerary visual language into a practical bone-and-arrow economy without copying the necropolis.

Island_142.secondary_feature: Suspended walkways, loom houses, cliff watchtowers, sealed spider galleries
Island_142.notes: A vertical Haunted Marches variant using bridges and towers to keep residents above dangerous ground.

Island_147.settlement_role: Mostly abandoned frontier with only a ranger-warden outpost
Island_147.secondary_feature: Overgrown palisades, ruined chapel, collapsed manor, warning beacons
Island_147.notes: Intentionally low-build island preserving evidence of failed settlement and making the region feel historically dangerous.

Island_087.settlement_role: Blackfen stilt capital and marsh-market center
Island_087.terrain_character: Wetlands, mangrove channels and unstable marsh ground
Island_087.secondary_feature: Great boardwalk, pile-built market hall, marsh shrine, raised council house
Island_087.lore_notes: Blackfen architecture uses pile foundations, lightweight upper structures, boardwalk spines, roofed docks and elevated communal buildings.
Island_087.notes: Dense network of boardwalks and water lanes rather than streets.

Island_056.primary_function: Mangrove timber support / boats / wetland transport
Island_056.secondary_feature: Long boatsheds, pole docks, drying racks, tidal slips
Island_056.notes: Blackfen carpentry adapted to boats and wet conditions; more open and industrial than the capital.

Island_069.settlement_role: Herbal marsh village and isolated witchworks
Island_069.secondary_feature: Herb gardens, crooked apothecary towers, raised brewing huts
Island_069.notes: Leans into Blackfen medicinal and superstitious traditions without turning the whole region into a haunted theme.

Island_110.settlement_role: Slime-basin work camp and raised processing village
Island_110.secondary_feature: Open slime basin, elevated walkways, wash platforms, storage lofts
Island_110.notes: All inhabited spaces stay elevated above the work basin.

Island_141.settlement_role: Sparse marsh hamlets and managed frog wetlands
Island_141.secondary_feature: Reed hides, low observation towers, breeding ponds, footbridges
Island_141.notes: Settlement yields to habitat rather than dominating it.

Island_100.secondary_feature: Raised garden beds, fungus sheds, drying huts, boardwalk farms
Island_100.notes: Shows Blackfen's quieter subsistence side and supplies specialty organic inputs.

Island_111.secondary_feature: Covered market bridge, cargo punts, raised inns, toll house
Island_111.notes: Grand Exchange influence appears in commerce, but everything remains low, wet and boat-oriented.

Island_054.settlement_role: Small salvage camp around older drowned ruins
Island_054.secondary_feature: Flooded foundations, half-sunken shrine, diver platforms, salvage crane
Island_054.notes: Historical layer showing that Blackfen settlement patterns changed as channels moved.

Island_066.secondary_feature: Pile-built cloisters, lantern boardwalk, bell pavilion, reed gardens
Island_066.notes: Blackfen architecture becomes formal and contemplative while remaining lightweight and elevated.

Island_133.secondary_feature: Channel markers, ferry sheds, guide hall, beacon poles
Island_133.notes: Functional infrastructure island connecting the region's maze of waterways.

Island_161.secondary_feature: Canopy platforms, hidden boardwalk, research hut
Island_161.notes: Intentionally underbuilt to preserve a genuinely wild wetland core.

Island_098.settlement_role: Small craft villages on long boardwalks
Island_098.secondary_feature: Weaving sheds, paper mills, reed drying racks, covered docks
Island_098.notes: A lighter domestic Blackfen settlement focused on craft rather than heavy production.

Island_144.secondary_feature: Gate tower, raised palisade, signal mast, floodgate
Island_144.notes: Blackfen defense uses water channels and narrow approaches instead of massive stone walls.

Island_086.settlement_role: Stone Highlands quarry capital and masonry center
Island_086.secondary_feature: Great quarry, masons' hall, terraced civic square, stone crane
Island_086.lore_notes: Stone Highlands architecture uses massive low walls, deep-set openings, retaining terraces, stepped streets and practical quarry-built civic halls.
Island_086.notes: Primary regional source of bulk stone and geological materials.

Island_103.primary_function: Cobblestone / stone generation and bulk processing
Island_103.secondary_feature: Water channels, generator halls, cutting yards, stone depots
Island_103.notes: Functional industry kept visually grounded in massive masonry rather than Engineer's Reach styling.

Island_121.secondary_feature: Test arches, bridge yard, retaining-wall school, stone guildhall
Island_121.notes: Refined engineering side of Stone Highlands culture and source of skilled builders.

Island_014.settlement_role: Dry-stone farm villages and shepherd routes
Island_014.secondary_feature: Terraced pasture, stone barns, boundary walls, hill shrine
Island_014.notes: Vernacular Stone Highlands life away from the quarries.

Island_015.secondary_feature: Cliff chapel, refuge hall, signal tower, switchback road
Island_015.notes: Uses the region's squat durable masonry in a more austere sacred and defensive form.

Island_160.secondary_feature: Block cranes, deep quays, stone warehouses, inclined haul road
Island_160.notes: Grand Exchange logistics adapted to monumental stone construction.

Island_083.settlement_role: Red Clay Basin capital and master ceramics city
Island_083.terrain_character: Mesas, clay gullies and kiln valleys
Island_083.secondary_feature: Great kiln court, potters' guild, terracotta market, shaded civic arcade
Island_083.lore_notes: Red Clay Basin architecture uses brick, terracotta and packed-earth masses, shallow roofs, shaded arcades and courtyards following mesa shelves.
Island_083.notes: Ceramics are both industry and art here.

Island_091.settlement_role: Terracotta works and color kiln town
Island_091.secondary_feature: Glaze yards, stepped kilns, pigment court, tiled arcades
Island_091.notes: Artisan Coast influence appears in finished goods but massing stays heavy and earthen.

Island_149.secondary_feature: Long kilns, drying yards, brick warehouses, worker courtyards
Island_149.notes: Practical industrial settlement built almost entirely from its own output.

Island_107.settlement_role: Potters' quarter city and workshop terraces
Island_107.secondary_feature: Courtyard studios, tile roofs, market stairs, communal kilns
Island_107.notes: Smaller-scale craft production makes this island feel inhabited and artistic rather than industrial.

Island_113.secondary_feature: Cistern plaza, arcaded bazaar, garden courts, low watchtower
Island_113.notes: Everyday Red Clay Basin urban life away from kilns.

Island_065.primary_function: Raw clay gathering / water-managed mud fields
Island_065.settlement_role: Small clay-field villages and processing compounds
Island_065.secondary_feature: Settling ponds, mud yards, drying walls, irrigation channels
Island_065.notes: Low-tech origin point for the ceramic economy.

Island_148.primary_function: Water storage / canals / industrial water supply
Island_148.secondary_feature: Reservoir, aqueduct arches, water court, distribution channels
Island_148.notes: Water engineering shapes the entire settlement and expresses the civilization's response to dry terrain.

Island_138.secondary_feature: Walled inn court, cargo yards, market gate, terracotta warehouses
Island_138.notes: Grand Exchange ideas translated into the Basin's courtyard and shade-oriented architecture.

Island_135.settlement_role: Small scholar camp among older mesa ruins
Island_135.secondary_feature: Buried courtyards, broken kiln complex, stepped temple ruins
Island_135.notes: Preserves an older architectural layer that modern Basin builders selectively imitate.

Island_080.settlement_role: Sunken Coast lagoon capital and principal fishing port
Island_080.terrain_character: Lagoons, tidal flats and shallow inlets
Island_080.secondary_feature: Tidal market, sea gates, stilted council hall, lagoon docks
Island_080.lore_notes: Sunken Coast architecture uses stilted quays, raised storehouses, tidal gates, seawalls and houses oriented around boat access.
Island_080.notes: Civic center built around water level and boat traffic rather than streets.

Island_101.settlement_role: Working fishing villages and processing docks
Island_101.secondary_feature: Fish houses, net lofts, smoker sheds, tidal pens
Island_101.notes: Everyday maritime economy with dense low stilt villages.

Island_114.primary_function: Kelp / sea vegetation / dried fuel support
Island_114.secondary_feature: Kelp racks, drying sheds, submerged fields, long piers
Island_114.notes: Cultivated seascape where farms extend into water rather than across land.

Island_112.settlement_role: Fortified salvage town beside controlled drowned waters
Island_112.secondary_feature: Diver towers, chain gates, salvage quays, floodlit watch piers
Island_112.notes: Sunken Coast danger is maritime; architecture controls channels and sightlines.

Island_118.secondary_feature: Tidal gates, water wheels, processing sheds, mill causeway
Island_118.notes: Strongest expression of practical tidal engineering.

Island_151.settlement_role: Small salvage village wrapped around a drowned former town
Island_151.secondary_feature: Submerged streets, broken sea wall, bell tower, diver camp
Island_151.notes: Visible historical disaster that explains why modern builders respect water so deeply.

Island_134.secondary_feature: Tall light tower, breakwater, rescue station, storm chapel
Island_134.notes: Compact maritime landmark marking the edge of safer waters.

Island_090.settlement_role: Crystal Deep subterranean capital and research center
Island_090.terrain_character: Deep caverns, geodes and ancient subterranean voids
Island_090.secondary_feature: Grand cavern hall, crystal galleries, suspended bridges, sealed sculk laboratory
Island_090.lore_notes: Crystal Deep architecture is carved rather than built: suspended bridges, precise geometry and monumental underground halls with controlled crystal light.
Island_090.notes: Main inhabited cavern complex built partly into older geometric ruins.

Island_009.secondary_feature: Geode galleries, resonance hall, cutting terraces, crystal vault
Island_009.notes: Architecture frames and protects geodes instead of burying them inside ordinary industrial buildings.

Island_155.secondary_feature: Observation bridges, sensor galleries, sealed laboratories, warning gates
Island_155.notes: Quiet routes and isolated chambers shape the architecture.

Island_023.settlement_role: Cavern rail junction and lift city
Island_023.secondary_feature: Suspended station, vertical lifts, bridge platforms, freight caverns
Island_023.notes: Crystal Deep geometry adapted to movement rather than research or mining.

Island_039.secondary_feature: Glow-berry terraces, moss gardens, water courts, grotto homes
Island_039.notes: Softer inhabited counterpoint to ominous deep research sites.

Island_131.settlement_role: Scholar camp on the edge of monumental ruins
Island_131.secondary_feature: Excavation bridges, archive hall, sealed ruin gates, survey towers
Island_131.notes: Modern construction stays visibly temporary beside older architecture.

Island_146.secondary_feature: Crystal chapel, reflection pools, hanging walkways, bell chamber
Island_146.notes: Formalizes the region's fascination with sound, light and geometry into a sacred tradition.

Island_154.settlement_role: Dripstone works and geological field station
Island_154.secondary_feature: Stalactite galleries, collection basins, survey bridges, rock archive
Island_154.notes: Keeps cave-geology production distinct from Stone Highlands surface quarry culture.

Island_016.secondary_feature: Gatehouse, descent stair, lift tower, expedition hostel
Island_016.notes: Architectural transition between surface traditions and fully subterranean Crystal Deep style.

Island_047.settlement_role: Volcano caldera capital and great foundry city
Island_047.terrain_character: Basalt slopes, caldera walls and lava-cut terraces
Island_047.secondary_feature: Great furnace hall, lava canals, basalt citadel, forge plaza
Island_047.lore_notes: Volcano architecture uses thick basalt masonry, vaulted hot-work halls, open lava channels, buttresses and heat-separated courtyards.
Island_047.notes: Industry and civic identity are inseparable.

Island_026.secondary_feature: Cauldron galleries, dripstone halls, heat channels, cistern vaults
Island_026.notes: Utilitarian Volcano settlement built around safe separation of heat and habitation.

Island_150.secondary_feature: Block yards, forge arcades, crane towers, cooling courts
Island_150.notes: Material-processing tradition without duplicating Ember Coast Nether-specific industries.

Island_115.primary_function: Foundry export / geothermal port / heavy shipping
Island_115.secondary_feature: Heat-shielded quays, cargo cranes, cooling basin, fortress warehouses
Island_115.notes: Maritime face of the Volcano where heavy industrial forms meet freight needs.

Island_097.settlement_role: Layered pirate capital and independent freeport
Island_097.terrain_character: Coves, cliffs and layered harbor slopes
Island_097.secondary_feature: Tavern quarter, improvised citadel, stacked docks, rope-bridge alleys
Island_097.lore_notes: Pirate Island architecture reuses ship timber and imported stone opportunistically, stacking additions over older structures so captured traditions remain visible.
Island_097.notes: Every era and borrowed building tradition should remain legible.

Island_064.secondary_feature: Dry docks, ship ribs, salvage yards, mast cranes, chandlers' row
Island_064.notes: Timberlands craft and Grand Exchange dock technology are borrowed but improvised into an unruly maritime workshop city.

Island_158.settlement_role: Hidden cove settlement and contraband depot
Island_158.secondary_feature: Sea caves, disguised warehouses, cliff stairs, signal fires
Island_158.notes: Sparse from open sea but dense inside concealed coves; the most secretive expression of Pirate culture.

Island_102.primary_function: Nether portal administration / Nether vegetation / civic support
Island_102.settlement_role: Ember Coast portal capital and fortified industrial city
Island_102.terrain_character: Volcanic coast, ash fields and portal-industrial enclaves
Island_102.secondary_feature: Portal bastion, warped/crimson garden courts, blackstone civic works, furnace causeways
Island_102.lore_notes: Ember Coast architecture uses severe blackstone/basalt complexes, protected portal courts, defensible streets and compartmentalized industrial districts; Volcano masonry is its strongest outside influence.
Island_102.notes: One of three multi-district Nether islands. Keep each production ecosystem visibly separated rather than blending everything into one factory.

Island_126.settlement_role: Fortress-factory island with separate gold/piglin and blaze/wither districts
Island_126.secondary_feature: Piglin exchange citadel, gold works, fortress-spire district, wither containment yards
Island_126.notes: Two distinct Nether ecosystems share one island but must have separate architecture, access routes and silhouettes. Gold district is mercantile-fortified; blaze/wither district is austere and fortress-like.

Island_136.settlement_role: Ash-coast industrial island with three separated production districts
Island_136.secondary_feature: Magma works and froglight towers; hoglin stockade settlement; basalt/blackstone quarry-fort
Island_136.notes: Three distinct districts linked by fortified causeways. Avoid a single mega-factory: each ecosystem should read as its own settlement adapted to its resource.

Island_096.settlement_role: Sapphire Coast reef capital and primary guardian-production city
Island_096.terrain_character: Coral shelf, reef channels and pale coastal terraces
Island_096.secondary_feature: Guardian monument district, sea towers, reef gardens, water arches
Island_096.lore_notes: Sapphire Coast architecture uses pale stone, prismarine accents, repeated arches over water, stepped seawalls and monumental marine complexes.
Island_096.notes: Underwater and shoreline spaces should feel like one continuous city.

Island_058.primary_function: Coral / reef stewardship / decorative marine resources
Island_058.secondary_feature: Coral gardens, low sea pavilions, glass-bottom walks, reef shrine
Island_058.notes: The softer ecological side of Sapphire Coast culture, with formal marine landscaping rather than heavy monument infrastructure.

Island_068.secondary_feature: Arcaded quays, sail lofts, customs tower, fish market
Island_068.notes: Grand Exchange mercantile ideas are translated into pale coastal masonry and water-facing arcades.

Island_127.settlement_role: Lighthouse city and prismarine workshop island
Island_127.secondary_feature: Great sea light, prismarine yards, channel towers, ceremonial sea gate
Island_127.notes: A prestigious maritime landmark whose structures are visible from long distance and unmistakably Sapphire Coast.

Island_085.settlement_role: Isles of Plenty tropical capital and primary creature-production ecosystem
Island_085.terrain_character: Tropical hills, fertile coasts and orchard belts
Island_085.secondary_feature: Open market pavilions, animal compounds, veranda civic hall, colorful waterfront
Island_085.lore_notes: Isles of Plenty architecture uses open structures, deep shade, high ventilated roofs, verandas, light raised foundations and lush courtyard compounds.
Island_085.notes: Main Passive Animal & Creature ecosystem, embedded in an inhabited tropical landscape rather than a farm complex.

Island_152.settlement_role: Tropical plantation villages and apiary district
Island_152.secondary_feature: Bamboo halls, sugar presses, melon terraces, bee gardens, shaded storage barns
Island_152.notes: Breadbasket organization is adapted to tropical crops, while building forms remain open, shaded and lightweight.

Island_137.settlement_role: Small coastal hamlets around a largely preserved tropical interior
Island_137.secondary_feature: Sanctuary trails, orchard compounds, beach shrine, ranger lodge
Island_137.notes: Deliberately less developed, giving the region a lush natural core and room for passive creatures to dominate the landscape.

Island_095.settlement_role: Transit Isles central interchange and transport capital
Island_095.secondary_feature: Grand terminal, rocket port, ferry basin, signal tower, traveler quarter
Island_095.lore_notes: Transit Isles architecture is infrastructure-first: terminals, bridgeheads, lighthouses, inns and warehouses use standardized wayfinding even while borrowing surface styles from every region.
Island_095.notes: Primary transportation nexus of the archipelago.

Island_008.settlement_role: Rail terminal city and maintenance yards
Island_008.secondary_feature: Long station hall, switching tower, maintenance sheds, viaduct approaches
Island_008.notes: Engineer's Reach structural ideas are borrowed, but the island is organized around passenger movement and clear navigation rather than manufacturing.

Island_010.primary_function: Rocket production / elytra staging / long-distance travel
Island_010.secondary_feature: Launch towers, fireworks works, flight hall, landing terraces
Island_010.notes: The most vertical Transit Isles settlement, but standardized signs, inns and transfer halls keep it culturally consistent with the region.

Island_036.settlement_role: Major lighthouse station with tiny keeper village
Island_036.secondary_feature: Great lighthouse, fog bell, signal mast, rescue boathouse
Island_036.notes: A small but iconic island whose architecture prioritizes visibility and orientation.

Island_063.primary_function: Cargo transfer / container-style sorting / intermodal freight
Island_063.secondary_feature: Cargo sheds, cranes, sorter depot, ferry ramps
Island_063.notes: Grand Exchange logistics are heavily borrowed, but circulation is clearer and more standardized than in the mercantile capital.

Island_052.settlement_role: Ferry city and maritime transfer hub
Island_052.secondary_feature: Ferry halls, covered piers, baggage warehouses, traveler inns
Island_052.notes: Former Convergence territory is folded into Transit Isles; architecture mixes regional influences but standardized platforms and wayfinding make the identity clear.

Island_116.settlement_role: Crossroads town for travelers between major routes
Island_116.secondary_feature: Large inn complex, repair yards, stables/vehicle sheds, market concourse
Island_116.notes: The most domestic Transit island: a place to stop, sleep and resupply rather than merely pass through.

Island_162.secondary_feature: Signal fortress, bridge towers, emergency harbor, pilot house
Island_162.notes: Transit architecture becomes defensive here, using imported Crownlands forms but retaining standardized navigation and movement logic.

Island_128.settlement_role: Shrouded Isles hidden capital with distinct Enderman and shulker/storage districts
Island_128.terrain_character: Remote fog islands, strange cliffs and concealed interior basins
Island_128.secondary_feature: Hidden observatory, impossible-looking towers, Enderman court, shulker vault quarter
Island_128.lore_notes: Shrouded Isles architecture uses sparse footprints, strong silhouettes, concealed access, unusual proportions and abstracted End-inspired forms; mainland forms feel familiar but subtly wrong.
Island_128.notes: Two End production ecosystems occupy separate districts so the capital remains mysterious rather than becoming one machine complex.

Island_071.primary_function: Chorus & Purpur; End Obsidian & special systems
Island_071.settlement_role: Remote End-material enclave with separate chorus/purpur and obsidian/special-system districts
Island_071.secondary_feature: Chorus gardens, purpur terraces, obsidian observatory, sealed experimental courts
Island_071.notes: The more alien of the two Shrouded islands. Settlement stays sparse, with long gaps of wilderness between distinct production compounds and hidden research sites.
